title: Picard group of a regular-local localization vanishes
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $f\in A$, and let $A_f$ be the localization of $A$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated projective $A_f$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $A_f$ the localization $P_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $(A_f)_{\mathfrak q}$-module of rank one. Then $P\cong A_f$ as $A_f$-modules. (These modules are the invertible $A_f$-modules, so this says $\operatorname{Pic}(A_f)=0$.)

proof.text: Prove the private helper invertible_of_prime_localizations: finite projectivity gives finite presentation. For each maximal ideal q, localization of the dual evaluation map identifies with evaluation of the localized module, via IsLocalizedModule.mapExtendScalars and IsLocalization.moduleTensorEquiv. The supplied rank-one linear equivalence makes that evaluation bijective. Mathlib bijective_of_isLocalized_maximal then shows evaluation is globally bijective, which is the definition of Module.Invertible. The explicit compatibility is checked on pure tensors in Lean.

Apply [lem-trf-localized-finite-module-spread] to P, obtaining a finite A-module M in the ring universe and an equivalence e : M_f ≃ P. Apply the existing source finite-projective-dimension theorem [lem-trf-regular-local-finite-projective-dimension] to M to obtain d with pd(M) ≤ d.

Transport projectivity from P to N=M_f along e. Apply [lem-trf-projective-localization-stably-free] to the canonical localization map M -> N. All universe requirements hold since M and its canonical localization have the ring universe. This makes N stably free. Transport invertibility from Step 1 along e as well.

Apply [lem-trf-stably-free-invertible-free] to N. Mathlib Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv turns its freeness into N ≃ A_f. Composing with e inverse gives P ≃ A_f. No assumption that f is nonzero or a nonunit is made.
